title: This 14-Year-Old Started a Nonprofit to Teach Kids Coding
summary:
What were you doing when you were 14? Abhijay Potluri, from Boxborough, Massachusetts, started a nonprofit called Kids Who Teach. He also helped organize a fundraiser for people affected by a fire near his home.

Abhijay has always liked figuring out how things work. During the COVID-19 pandemic, he learned coding. He realized kids could build things that actually help people. So he started teaching coding, public speaking, and problem-solving to kids in India, Indonesia, Uganda, and the U.S.

When a fire broke out near his home, he saw families struggling. Some kids in his school became homeless. He helped raise money for them. "What stuck with me was seeing every age show up: fourth graders donating next to adults," he says. "It taught me that a small community can make a real difference."

Abhijay is busy. School, sports, and his projects all pile up. But he plans his day and gets things done. He says the hardest part is figuring out where to start. "Once you make a plan or a timeline, it gets a lot easier," he says. "You just need to take the first step."

People sometimes think kids can't make real change. That bothers Abhijay. But he's proof they can.
why_it_matters: It shows that you don't have to be a grown-up to help your community — a plan, a first step and a little time can turn an idea into something real.
